stem: Ekta has nine odd-numbered cards. She wants to place all nine cards so that their sum is exactly $50$.

parts.text: What can she decide before trying any cases?

options.text: The sum of nine odd numbers is odd, so it cannot equal $50$.
The sum of nine odd numbers is even, so $50$ is reachable.
Parity does not apply until she first chooses which cards make the total.
Any nine positive cards can make $50$ if their sizes are small enough.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: An odd count of odd addends makes an odd sum, but $50$ is even, so no arrangement works.

teacher.key_rationale: Nine odd addends force an odd sum; 50 is even, so the target is impossible before trying cases. Calling that sum even reverses parity. Saying parity waits for selection omits the forced-parity condition. Size alone is outside the parity hinge.
